validation.status: candidate; close functionality asserted; native cleanup failures retained

offline_smoke.result: Opened the fixture, created all five annotation types, saved and reopened them; normal browser exit.

native_visible_close.environment: ObReader-Apple-Test vault with mobile emulation; not a physical iPad test.
native_visible_close.functional_assertions: All six scenarios were recorded with a real visible tab close button. Edited cases began at revision 2, confirmed revision 0, and annotation storage size 1; the saved PDF contained one Square. In write-failure cases the original PDF bytes remained unchanged and at least one recovery PDF parsed successfully with one Square and revision-2 recovery metadata. Clean cases retained the original PDF bytes and no Square.
native_visible_close.overall_run_status: Both six-scenario runs exited with code 1 during test cleanup because one Reader view remained. The first JSON says status=passed despite its restoreError; that status is not treated as a successful run. The second JSON reports failed. Functional assertions are reported separately from process exit.
native_visible_close.independent_cleanup: A later cleanup record confirms only the owned unedited fixture Reader was detached, and a separate restore record confirms mobile=false and views=0.
native_visible_close.earlier_attempts: Earlier native attempts are retained. The first did not reach the close scenarios because the Square/revision setup assertion failed; later attempts failed page-visibility or precondition checks before close assertions. They are not counted as successful close checks.

default_suite.note: The focused close suite, package runtime suite, offline smoke test, and native close scenarios are recorded separately; no full default-suite pass is claimed.

assessment.retracted_finding: The earlier close-deadline/checkpoint timer-race concern was retracted after reviewing request ordering: an in-flight checkpoint necessarily starts before close intent, and the Viewer manual-save path waits on syncCheckpointPromise.
assessment.conclusion: The reviewed close/quiesce and queued-only cancellation paths have no blocking source defect. Six real-button functional scenarios are evidenced for desktop and mobile emulation, including saving revision-2 edits and preserving a valid recovery PDF on injected write failure. Both native scenario processes nevertheless exited 1 on leftover-view cleanup; independent cleanup later confirmed the test vault returned to desktop mode with zero Reader views. These results do not establish a clean native-run exit or physical iPad behavior.
